title: Compare without ==
intro: `equals` compares the text, case and all; `equalsIgnoreCase` lets upper and lower case match; `compareTo` says which comes first: negative, zero or positive. Judge each call.

rightEach.equals: Case counts for `equals`: an upper-case letter is a different character from its lower-case twin.

rounds.right: Same letters, different case: `equals` says `false`, `equalsIgnoreCase` says `true`.

why.equals: `equals` compares character by character, and case counts: at index {k}, {ca} and {cb} are different characters.
why.equalsIgnoreCase: `equalsIgnoreCase` lets each upper-case letter match its lower-case twin, and every pair here matches that way.

rounds.prompt: Negative means the first comes first. Judge the sign of each `compareTo`.
rounds.right: Swap the two sides and the sign flips; compare a String with itself and you get 0.

why.compareTo.differ: Compare from the left: the first pair of characters that differ decides. At index {k}, {ca} is {na} and {cb} is {nb}, and the answer is their difference.
why.compareTo.prefix: One String is the start of the other, so no character differs before the shorter one runs out: the lengths decide, {la} minus {lb}.
why.compareTo.same: Every character matches and so do the lengths: a String compared with itself gives 0.

rounds.prompt: Sort `{name}` the way `compareTo` orders Strings: click two boxes to swap them.
rounds.right: Sorted in {verdict} A word that starts another comes first; otherwise the first different letter decides.

why.wasted: Neither word landed in its place. Compare from the first letter: the word `compareTo` puts first belongs in box 0.

rounds.prompt: `cmd` might be `null`. What does each call do?
rounds.right: Put the literal first: `"pause".equals(cmd)` is safe, because a literal is never `null`. Called on `null`, `equals` can't run at all.

why.throws: `"pause"` is a literal, never `null`, so `equals` can run. Given `null` to compare with, it simply answers `false`.
why.equals: `cmd` holds `null`: there is no text for `"pause"` to match, so the answer can't be `true`.
why.equals.npe: `cmd` holds `null`: there is no object to call `equals` on, so Java throws a `NullPointerException` before comparing anything.
